# Slides

::: {.doc-lead}
Build a presentation from the plots and figures in your project. The stage is the figure editor — the same tools, Inspector and live plots — with steps, an Animator and exports that play anywhere.
:::

Shortcuts are written for Linux and Windows; on macOS, **Ctrl** is **⌘** and **Alt** is **⌥**.

## Decks and the filmstrip {#decks-and-the-filmstrip}

The deck list sits above the filmstrip: create (**+ New deck**), duplicate, or remove decks —
each is one readable file in the project. The filmstrip shows live thumbnails: drag to
reorder, duplicate or delete from a thumb, **+ Add slide** for a new slide (layouts seed
starter text — title, section, two-column, or *blank* for a clean stage), and **+ Preset**
inserts a slide from your machine-global **slide preset library** (save any slide there from
the Slide panel — its animation, background, and media travel with it).

The right rail switches between four panels:

- **Object** edits the selected object.
- **Animation** edits the selected effect.
- **Slide** holds the slide's name, background, transition and speaker notes.
- **Deck** sets the **theme** and the **stage size** (16:9, 4:3 or 16:10). There are seven
  built-in themes: *Flux Dark*, *Flux Light*, *Paper*, *Midnight*, *Slate*, *Sepia* and *Contrast*.

**Ctrl+Shift+B** hides the right rail, and **Ctrl+B** hides the left rail (the filmstrip or
the Plots view) when no text is selected. Drag the inner edge of either rail to resize it.

## Place a plot from the Plots rail {#the-plots-rail}

The left rail has two views. **Slides** holds the deck list and the filmstrip. **Plots** is the
same plot gallery and live dissections pane the Figure workspace has: a searchable gallery on
top (see [Plot gallery](/docs/plot-gallery.html#getting-plots-in)) and, below it, the
[dissections](/docs/dissections.html) of the plot you last clicked. **Alt+G** switches to Plots
with the cursor in its search box (it also opens a hidden rail); **Alt+G** again returns to the
filmstrip. The two views keep their own widths.

- **Double-click** a plot, or press **Enter**, to place it on the active slide. A **→** line at
  the top of the rail names the slide that will receive it; click it to switch slides.
  **Drag** a plot onto the stage to place it where you let go, at the size it will land.
- Click a plot on the stage and the rail shows its dissections. The gallery marks the plots
  already on this slide, and **⋯ → Show only → Unused** lists the plots on no slide of this
  deck yet.
- Type **`_vid`** in the search box to open **`_videos`**: clips show their poster frames and
  place like plots. A clip that needs converting shows its progress at the top of the rail,
  with **Cancel**. Clips come from this project only; the global library lists plots, not
  clips. See [Video clips](/docs/slide-media.html#video-clips).
- **Shift+Alt+G**, or the toolbar's **Plots & videos**, opens the full gallery in its own
  window, with larger previews and **Pin open** for inserting several plots in a row.
- During a **Become** pick, a plot placed from the rail joins the pick (the pick switches to
  Add mode, exactly as when you draw something); **Enter** and **Space** in the rail place and
  preview, and never confirm the pick. See [Become](/docs/transforms.html#become).
- **F5** presents from the rail too.

<!-- MEDIA: Alt+G opens the Plots view beside the stage; a plot is dragged onto the stage and lands at its final size; clicking it fills the dissections pane below the gallery. -->

## Steps and editing destination {#steps-and-editing-destination}

A presentation is a sequence of named **steps** (called beats in the deck file and commands).
**Start** is the initial presentation frame. Each later step runs **On click**, **With previous**,
or **After previous** with a chosen delay (an After previous step waits 150 ms by default). The
step strip always stays visible while the timeline shows the selected step's effects.


<figure class="doc-figure"><a href="/assets/media/docs/slides-easing-workspace.png" data-enlarge data-caption="The stage, selected animation and timeline stay visible together. Design edits the starting objects; Edit after step shapes a later state."><img src="/assets/media/docs/slides-easing-workspace.png" alt="Flux Slides showing the six-curve comparison, with Design and Edit after step controls above the stage." width="2800" height="2000" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>The stage, selected animation and timeline stay visible together. Design edits the starting objects; Edit after step shapes a later state. Click to enlarge.</figcaption></figure>

The bar above the stage states where your edits go:

- **Design** edits the original slide objects.
- **Edit after step N** shows the result of every step up to N. Move, resize, recolour,
  rewrite or restyle an object to create or update a Change at **that exact step**; earlier
  steps stay intact. Adding, deleting, grouping and renaming objects are structural edits to
  the slide itself, whichever destination is chosen.

Selecting a different step browses its effects; it does not silently change the editing
destination. Choose **Edit after step N** when you want to shape the newly selected step.

**Show hidden** displays objects and plot parts that are hidden at the current point (they
have disappeared, or they are hand-off destinations that have not landed yet) as faint,
selectable ghosts. Turn it on to edit a hidden object or to add an **Appear** effect to it at a
later step. Turn it off to remove hidden objects from the canvas, selection and snapping, so you
can work on the objects underneath. Ghost copies do not exist before the step that creates them,
so they stay absent even with Show hidden on. The setting changes only your editing view; it
never deletes objects or changes what Present and the exports show.

**Fit** keeps the whole stage visible as you resize the dock and rails; manual zoom or pan
keeps your chosen view instead.

## Animate the slide {#animate-the-slide}

**Animate ⏱** opens the Animator, a dock below the stage with the step strip, a millisecond
ruler and one lane per effect. Select something on the stage (**Ctrl+click** drills to a plot
part), then choose what happens to it at the selected step:

| Button | What it adds | Details |
|---|---|---|
| **Appear** (**Ctrl+Shift+A**) | An entrance. Text rises in, shapes and arrows grow in, lines and paths draw on | [Choose an effect](/docs/animation.html#appearances) |
| **Transform ▾** | **Change** (**Ctrl+Shift+C**) a new state of the object; **Ghost…** (**Ctrl+Alt+G**) copies that move independently; **Become** (**B**) another object or plot parts | [Transforms](/docs/transforms.html#transforms) |
| **Emphasize** | A **pulse**: a calm swell and return. **Highlight**, **Dim** and **Circle it** are in the Effect menu | [Emphasis](/docs/animation.html#appearances) |
| **Disappear** (**Ctrl+Shift+D**) | An exit. Shapes shrink away, text and plots fade, lines draw off | [Choose an effect](/docs/animation.html#appearances) |
| **Focus** / **Unfocus** | Dim everything but the selection to 30 %; on a later step, bring it all back | [Focus on one thing](/docs/animation.html#focus) |
| **✨ Auto-animate** | A plot's whole build in three clicks: **Axes & grid**, **Data**, **Legend & annotations** | [Auto-animate a plot](/docs/animation.html#auto-animate) |
| **🎥 Zoom** / **⤢ Reset** | A camera move toward the selection, and back to the full slide | [Camera](/docs/transforms.html#camera-zoom-vs-fly) |

New effects start at a measured pace — entrances 0.7 s, exits 0.5 s, a Change or Become 1.2 s —
on a smooth curve; [Default timing](/docs/animation.html#default-timing) lists them all. The
Animator's lanes, alignment keys, easing editor, reusable styles and follow-timing links are
described in [Animation and timing](/docs/animation.html).

## Align and arrange on the stage {#align-and-arrange-on-slides}

The stage shares the Figure workspace's drawing and layout tools, with the same keys: **V**
select, **K** scale, **H** hand, **T** text, **Alt+R** rectangle, **O** ellipse, **L** line,
**Shift+L** arrow, **P** pen, and **R** for the [X-ray](/docs/plot-editing.html#x-ray) of a
selected plot.

- **A** opens **Align & Arrange** with Align active; **Alt+T** opens it with Arrange active.
  Both panes stay visible, and **Space** switches which one the keyboard drives. A selection
  shows pink gap guides directly, spacing is signed (a negative value overlaps), the selection
  pin opens a persistent **Keep fixed** chooser, and **1/2/3** choose start, centre or end on
  the gap you are editing or hovering. **Enter** applies and **Esc** cancels. The panel is
  described in the Figure guide: [Align & Arrange](/docs/figure-layout.html#align-and-arrange).
- The Animator keeps its own keys: with the Animator focused, **Alt+A** / **Alt+D** align
  effects' starts and ends rather than objects.
- **Connectors and labels stick to shapes**, as in Figure: a line end released on a shape
  follows it (a dashed outline marks the target while you drag; **Settings → Figure →
  Connectors stick to shapes** turns this off), and the Inspector's **Sticks to** row shows or
  changes the attachment. When the shape moves at a step, what is stuck to it moves with it —
  see [Connectors and labels follow what they stick to](/docs/transforms.html#connectors-follow).
  A deck that holds a stuck element is saved in a newer format, which older versions of Flux
  cannot open.

## Between figures and slides {#between-figures-and-slides}

**Send to deck…** (in the Figure workspace's Inspector) turns a figure into a slide.
**Send to canvas…** (in the Slide panel) turns a slide into a figure, which becomes citable as
`@fig-…` like any other. The copied composition is independently editable. Plot source data
stays linked unless you deliberately freeze a usage, and a later source refresh preserves your
slide-specific layout.

Decks remember the accepted intrinsic size of linked assets so regeneration preserves the
same placement scale whether the deck stays open or is reopened later. An older deck without
that baseline adopts the currently accepted size once; Flux cannot reconstruct dimensions
that were never saved.

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

| Symptom | Cause → fix |
|---|---|
| The animation shortcuts (such as **Ctrl+Shift+A**) do nothing | The Animator is closed → open it with **Animate ⏱** first |
| **Alt+R** draws a rectangle instead of opening the X-ray | The X-ray moved to **R**, and **Alt+R** is now the rectangle tool (the arrow tool is **Shift+L**) → press **R** with a plot selected |
| A plot Become fades a series instead of morphing its data | Continuous data motion requires shared series ids, supported data and matching axis scales. A series without a tweenable counterpart fades on its own (the Animation inspector lists it); only an SVG without semantic IDs crossfades as a whole. |
| An animation issue appears | Select the issue to inspect the effect, then retarget missing objects/parts or adjust overlapping timing |
| A shape becomes text and the letters land as boxes ("No readable outlines for …") | Flux cannot read letter outlines from the text's font. Gelasio, the bundled theme font, ships only as a web font, and a browser preview has no access to installed fonts → set the text in an installed font (Georgia, Arial, …). Until then the boxes still land on each letter and fade into the text |
| An older Flux refuses to open the deck | The deck uses a newer format because it holds a stuck connector or label, or a stagger ordered **radial** → open it with the current version |
| "Couldn't open that deck — its file may be missing or corrupt." appears while an agent edits the deck | Older versions of Flux could mistake a reload that the agent's next edit overtook for a damaged file → update Flux. The deck on disk is intact, so reopening it shows the agent's version |
| Present shows placeholder "Title / Subtitle" text | The slide was created with a starter layout → delete the starters, or use the *blank* layout when composing by hand |
